claim: Trained immunity is the long-term functional reprogramming of innate immune cells, which results in altered responses toward a secondary challenge.
source: Trained immunity is the long-term functional reprogramming of innate immune cells, which results in altered responses toward a secondary challenge.
evidence: This is a definitional statement presented in the abstract that establishes the concept of trained immunity.

claim: Indoxyl sulfate (IS) induces trained immunity in monocytes via epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, resulting in augmented cytokine production.
source: Here, we demonstrate that IS induces trained immunity in monocytes via epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, resulting in augmented cytokine production.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study as stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) contributes to IS-trained immunity by enhancing the expression of arachidonic acid (AA) metabolism-related genes such as ALOX5 and ALOX5AP.
source: Mechanistically, the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) contributes to IS-trained immunity by enhancing the expression of arachidonic acid (AA) metabolism-related genes such as arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase (ALOX5) and ALOX5 activating protein (ALOX5AP).
evidence: This mechanistic finding is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data including RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, and immunoblot analyses.

claim: Inhibition of AhR during IS training suppresses the induction of IS-trained immunity.
source: Inhibition of AhR during IS training suppresses the induction of IS-trained immunity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data using GNF351, an AhR antagonist, shown in Figure 4.

claim: Monocytes from end-stage renal disease (ESRD) patients have increased ALOX5 expression.
source: Monocytes from end-stage renal disease (ESRD) patients have increased ALOX5 expression and after 6 days training, they exhibit enhanced TNF-α and IL-6 production to lipopolysaccharide (LPS).
evidence: This finding is stated in the abstract and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6E-H.

claim: Monocytes from ESRD patients exhibit enhanced TNF-α and IL-6 production to LPS after 6 days training.
source: Monocytes from end-stage renal disease (ESRD) patients have increased ALOX5 expression and after 6 days training, they exhibit enhanced TNF-α and IL-6 production to lipopolysaccharide (LPS).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6A-C.

claim: Healthy control-derived monocytes trained with uremic sera from ESRD patients exhibit increased production of TNF-α and IL-6.
source: Furthermore, healthy control-derived monocytes trained with uremic sera from ESRD patients exhibit increased production of TNF-α and IL-6.
evidence: This finding is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G-I.

claim: IS-trained mice had increased production of TNF-α after in vivo LPS stimulation compared to control mice.
source: Consistently, IS-trained mice and their splenic myeloid cells had increased production of TNF-α after in vivo and ex vivo LPS stimulation compared to that of control mice.
evidence: This in vivo finding is stated in the abstract and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6J.

claim: Splenic myeloid cells from IS-trained mice had increased production of TNF-α after ex vivo LPS stimulation compared to control mice.
source: Consistently, IS-trained mice and their splenic myeloid cells had increased production of TNF-α after in vivo and ex vivo LPS stimulation compared to that of control mice.
evidence: This ex vivo finding is stated in the abstract and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6K.

claim: Trained immunity of monocytes and macrophages is the long-term functional reprogramming elicited by an initial primary insult, mainly pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs), which leads to an altered response towards a subsequent, unrelated secondary insult after the return to a homeostatic state.
source: Compared with classical epitope-specific adaptive immunological memory based on an antigen-receptor, trained immunity of monocytes and macrophages is the long-term functional reprogramming elicited by an initial primary insult, mainly pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs), which leads to an altered response towards a subsequent, unrelated secondary insult after the return to a homeostatic state (Netea et al., 2016; Netea et al., 2020).
evidence: This definitional statement is supported by citations to previous literature (Netea et al., 2016; Netea et al., 2020).

claim: Exposure of monocytes or macrophages to Candida albicans, fungal cell wall component β-glucan, or Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine enhances their subsequent responses to unrelated pathogens or pathogen components such as lipopolysaccharide (LPS).
source: It has been well demonstrated that exposure of monocytes or macrophages to Candida albicans, fungal cell wall component β-glucan, or Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine enhances their subsequent responses to unrelated pathogens or pathogen components such as lipopolysaccharide (LPS) (Arts et al., 2016b; Bekkering et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies (Arts et al., 2016b; Bekkering et al., 2018).

claim: The induction of trained immunity is associated with the interaction of epigenetic modifications and metabolic rewiring, which can last for prolonged periods of time.
source: The induction of trained immunity is associated with the interaction of epigenetic modifications and metabolic rewiring, which can last for prolonged periods of time (Netea et al., 2016; Netea et al., 2020; Bekkering et al., 2018; Cheng et al., 2014; Saeed et al., 2014; Christ et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Certain metabolites derived from the upregulation of different metabolic pathways triggered by primary insult can influence enzymes involved in remodeling the epigenetic landscape of cells.
source: Mechanistically, certain metabolites derived from the upregulation of different metabolic pathways triggered by primary insult can influence enzymes involved in remodeling the epigenetic landscape of cells.
evidence: This mechanistic explanation is presented as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Epigenetic changes lead to specific changes in histone markers, such as histone 3 lysine 4 trimethylation (H3K4me3) or histone 3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac), which regulate genes resulting in a more rapid and stronger response upon a subsequent, unrelated secondary insult.
source: This leads to specific changes in epigenetic histone markers, such as histone 3 lysine 4 trimethylation (H3K4me3) or histone 3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac), which regulate genes resulting in a more rapid and stronger response upon a subsequent, unrelated secondary insult (Netea et al., 2016; Netea et al., 2020; Arts et al., 2016b; Saeed et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Long non-coding RNAs induce epigenetic reprogramming via the histone methyltransferase, MLL1.
source: In addition, it has been recently reported that long non-coding RNAs induce epigenetic reprogramming via the histone methyltransferase, MLL1.
evidence: This statement is presented as a recent finding from the literature.

claim: Transcription factors such as Runx1 regulate the induction of proinflammatory cytokines following the secondary insult.
source: Subsequently, transcription factors such as Runx1 regulate the induction of proinflammatory cytokines following the secondary insult (Fanucchi et al., 2019; Edgar et al., 2021; Jentho et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Trained immunity likely evolved as a beneficial process for non-specific protection from future secondary infections.
source: Many studies have provided evidence that trained immunity likely evolved as a beneficial process for non-specific protection from future secondary infections (Netea et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Augmented immune responses resulting from trained immunity is potentially relevant to deleterious outcomes in immune-mediated and chronic inflammatory diseases such as autoimmune diseases, allergy, and atherosclerosis.
source: However, it has also been suggested that augmented immune responses resulting from trained immunity is potentially relevant to deleterious outcomes in immune-mediated and chronic inflammatory diseases such as autoimmune diseases, allergy, and atherosclerosis (Christ et al., 2018; Edgar et al., 2021; Bekkering et al., 2014; van der Valk et al., 2016; Arts et al., 2018; Mulder et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: OxLDL, lipoprotein a (Lpa), uric acid, hyperglycemia, and the Western diet have been identified as endogenous sterile insults that induce trained immunity in human monocytes via epigenetic reprogramming.
source: In support of this idea, oxLDL, lipoprotein a (Lpa), uric acid, hyperglycemia, and the Western diet have all been recently identified as endogenous sterile insults that induce trained immunity in human monocytes via epigenetic reprogramming (Christ et al., 2018; Edgar et al., 2021; Bekkering et al., 2014; van der Valk et al., 2016; Cabău et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to recent literature.

claim: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is recognized as a major non-communicable disease with increasing worldwide prevalence.
source: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is recognized as a major non-communicable disease with increasing worldwide prevalence (Chen et al., 2019; Couser et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Loss of renal function in CKD patients causes the accumulation of over 100 uremic toxins.
source: Loss of renal function in CKD patients causes the accumulation of over 100 uremic toxins, which are closely associated with cardiovascular risk and mortality due to their ability to generate oxidative stress and a proinflammatory cytokine milieu (Vanholder et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Uremic toxins are closely associated with cardiovascular risk and mortality due to their ability to generate oxidative stress and a proinflammatory cytokine milieu.
source: Loss of renal function in CKD patients causes the accumulation of over 100 uremic toxins, which are closely associated with cardiovascular risk and mortality due to their ability to generate oxidative stress and a proinflammatory cytokine milieu (Vanholder et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death among patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD).
source: Reflecting this, cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death among patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD; Kato et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Indoxyl sulfate (IS) is a major uremic toxin derived from dietary tryptophan via fermentation of gut microbiota.
source: Indoxyl sulfate (IS) is a major uremic toxin derived from dietary tryptophan via fermentation of gut microbiota (Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: IS is poorly cleared by hemodialysis.
source: Since it is poorly cleared by hemodialysis, IS is one of the uremic toxins present at higher than normal concentrations in the serum of CKD patients (Duranton et al., 2012; Lim et al., 2021)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: IS is one of the uremic toxins present at higher than normal concentrations in the serum of CKD patients.
source: Since it is poorly cleared by hemodialysis, IS is one of the uremic toxins present at higher than normal concentrations in the serum of CKD patients (Duranton et al., 2012; Lim et al., 2021)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: IS is associated with the progression of CKD and the development of CKD-related complications such as CVD.
source: IS is one of the uremic toxins present at higher than normal concentrations in the serum of CKD patients (Duranton et al., 2012; Lim et al., 2021) and is associated with the progression of CKD and the development of CKD-related complications such as CVD (Gao and Liu, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: IS promotes the production of proinflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and IL-1β by monocytes and macrophages through aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) signaling and organic anion transporting polypeptides 2B1 (OATP2B1)-Dll4-Notch Signaling.
source: We and others have shown that IS promotes the production of proinflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α and IL-1β by monocytes and macrophages through aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) signaling and organic anion transporting polypeptides 2B1 (OATP2B1)-Dll4-Notch Signaling (Kim et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2019; Nakano et al., 2019)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies including the authors' own work.

claim: Pretreatment with IS greatly increases TNF-α production by human macrophages in response to a low dose of LPS.
source: Moreover, pretreatment with IS greatly increases TNF-α production by human macrophages in response to a low dose of LPS (Kim et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: Preincubation of monocytes with IS led to enhanced production of TNF-α upon LPS stimulation.
source: Preincubation of monocytes with IS led to enhanced production of TNF-α, a major monocyte/macrophage-derived inflammatory cytokine, upon LPS stimulation.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 10 ng/ml of LPS significantly increased both TNF-α and IL-6 secretion in IS-trained macrophages.
source: Since 10 ng/ml of LPS significantly increased both TNF-α and IL-6 secretion in IS-trained macrophages (Figure 1B), we used this concentration of LPS in subsequent experiments.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A clinically relevant concentration of IS in severe CKD has been reported in the range from 0.5 to 1.0 mmol/L.
source: A clinically relevant concentration of IS in severe CKD has reported the range from 0.5 to 1.0 mmol/L (Vanholder et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The preincubation effect of IS on cytokine production was observed at a concentration as low as 250 μM, which is the average IS concentration in patients with ESRD in the authors' cohort.
source: The preincubation effect of IS on cytokine production was observed at a concentration as low as 250 μM, which is the average IS concentration in patients with ESRD in our cohort (Figure 1C; Kim et al., 2019).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1C and citation to previous work.

claim: Preincubation with other protein-bound uremic toxins (PBUTs), such as p-cresyl sulfate (PCS), hippuric acid (HA), indole 3-acetic acid (IAA), and kynurenic acid (KA), did not cause increased secretion of TNF-α or IL-6 in response to LPS stimulation.
source: Unlike IS, preincubation with other protein-bound uremic toxins (PBUTs), such as p-cresyl sulfate (PCS), hippuric acid (HA), indole 3-acetic acid (IAA), and kynurenic acid (KA), did not cause increased secretion of TNF-α or IL-6 in response to LPS stimulation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There was no obvious effect on cell viability following pre-incubation of macrophages with 1000 μM of IS after a subsequent 5-day culture in human serum or after LPS stimulation.
source: In addition, there was no obvious effect on cell viability following pre-incubation of macrophages with 1000 μM of IS after a subsequent 5-day culture in human serum or after LPS stimulation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The enhanced cytokine production of IS-trained macrophages was not attributable to potassium derived from IS potassium salt.
source: We also found that the enhanced cytokine production of IS-trained macrophages was not attributable to potassium derived from IS potassium salt (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The increased TNF-α and IL-6 production in IS-trained macrophages was not limited to LPS stimulation, as similar phenomena were observed following stimulation with Pam3cys, a TLR1/2 agonist.
source: Moreover, the increased TNF-α and IL-6 production in IS-trained macrophages was not limited to LPS stimulation, as similar phenomena were observed following stimulation with Pam3cys, a TLR1/2 agonist (Figure 1D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: β-glucan-pretreated macrophages exhibit a prototypic feature of trained immunity, characterized by enhanced production of inflammatory cytokines upon restimulation with heterologous stimuli, LPS or Pam3cys.
source: β-glucan-pretreated macrophages exhibit a prototypic feature of trained immunity, characterized by enhanced production of inflammatory cytokines upon restimulation with heterologous stimuli, LPS or Pam3cys (Cheng et al., 2014; Bekkering et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The level of TNF-α secreted by IS-trained macrophages was comparable with that secreted by β-glucan-trained macrophages.
source: As seen in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, the level of TNF-α secreted by IS-trained macrophages was comparable with that secreted by β-glucan-trained macrophages, although β-glucan had a more potent effect on IL-6 production than did IS
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: β-glucan had a more potent effect on IL-6 production than did IS.
source: As seen in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, the level of TNF-α secreted by IS-trained macrophages was comparable with that secreted by β-glucan-trained macrophages, although β-glucan had a more potent effect on IL-6 production than did IS
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: There was a notable increase in the mRNA expression of IL-1β and MCP-1 (CCL2) observed in IS-trained macrophages.
source: Furthermore, alongside elevated TNF-α and IL-6 expressions, there was a notable increase in the mRNA expression of IL-1β and MCP-1 (CCL2) observed in IS-trained macrophages, concomitant with a significant reduction in IL-10, a cytokine known for its anti-inflammatory properties, within the same cellular context (Figure 1E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: There was a significant reduction in IL-10 in IS-trained macrophages.
source: Furthermore, alongside elevated TNF-α and IL-6 expressions, there was a notable increase in the mRNA expression of IL-1β and MCP-1 (CCL2) observed in IS-trained macrophages, concomitant with a significant reduction in IL-10, a cytokine known for its anti-inflammatory properties, within the same cellular context (Figure 1E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Alterations in protein levels of IL-1β, MCP-1, and IL-10 mirrored the observed mRNA expressions in IS-trained macrophages.
source: Correspondingly, alterations in their protein levels mirrored the observed mRNA expressions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Circulating monocytes have been identified as a major immune cell subset that responds to IS in the serum of ESRD patients.
source: Circulating monocytes have been identified as a major immune cell subset that responds to IS in the serum of ESRD patients (Kim et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: Training with pooled uremic serum of ESRD patients increased the production of TNF-α and IL-6 upon re-stimulation with LPS compared to monocytes treated with the pooled sera of HCs.
source: Training with pooled uremic serum of ESRD patients increased the production of TNF-α and IL-6 upon re-stimulation with LPS compared to monocytes treated with the pooled sera of HCs (Figure 1G–I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1G-I.

claim: Expression of IL-1β and MCP-1 mRNA was augmented by training with the pooled uremic sera of ESRD patients.
source: In addition, expression of IL-1β and MCP-1 mRNA was also augmented by training with the pooled uremic sera of ESRD patients (Figure 1I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Training with IS led to an enhanced extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) as a measure of lactate production, indicating increased glycolysis and glycolysis capacity.
source: Assessment of the metabolic profile of IS-trained macrophages on day 6 (prior to re-stimulation with LPS) showed that training with IS led to an enhanced extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) as a measure of lactate production, indicating increased glycolysis and glycolysis capacity (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by Seahorse metabolic analysis data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Basal and maximal respiration and ATP production gauged by the oxygen consumption rate (OCR) were increased in IS-trained macrophages compared to non-trained cells.
source: Moreover, basal and maximal respiration and ATP production gauged by the oxygen consumption rate (OCR) were also increased compared to that of non-trained cells (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by Seahorse metabolic analysis data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Enhanced glycolysis and glycolytic capacity in IS-trained cells remained higher even after re-stimulation with LPS.
source: Enhanced glycolysis and glycolytic capacity in IS-trained cells remained higher even after re-stimulation with LPS (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B)
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: 2-DG completely inhibited the augmented production of TNF-α and IL-6 in IS-trained macrophages in response to re-stimulation with LPS.
source: 2-DG completely inhibited the augmented production of TNF-α and IL-6 in IS-trained macrophages in response to re-stimulation with LPS (Figure 2E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: IS-trained macrophages exhibit enhanced H3K4me3 of TNFA and IL6 promoters by day 6 after treatment with 1000 μM of IS.
source: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-qPCR data illustrate that IS-trained macrophages exhibit enhanced H3K4me3 of TNFA and IL6 promoters by day 6 after treatment with 1000 μM of IS (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: IS-mediated enrichment of H3K4me3 was maintained even after secondary stimulation with LPS compared with non-trained cells.
source: Moreover, IS-mediated enrichment of H3K4me3 was maintained even after secondary stimulation with LPS compared with non-trained cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: MTA reversed the production of TNF-α and IL-6 in IS-trained macrophages upon LPS stimulation to baseline.
source: When IS-trained macrophages were pretreated with 5'-methylthioadenosine (MTA), a non-selective methyltransferase inhibitor, their production of TNF-α and IL-6 upon LPS stimulation was reversed to baseline (Figure 3C)
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Metabolic rewiring influences epigenetic modification in IS-trained immunity.
source: To explore the potential regulation of IS-induced epigenetic modification by metabolic rewiring, we examined the enrichment of H3K4me3 at the promoters of TNFA and IL6 subsequent to treatment with 2-DG (Figure 3D). Our findings suggest that metabolic rewiring influences epigenetic modification, implicating the participation of metabolites.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Heightened enrichment of H3K4me3 at the promoter regions of HK2 and PFKP, pivotal genes associated with glycolysis, was observed in IS-trained macrophages.
source: Additionally, heightened enrichment of H3K4me3 at the promoter regions of HK2 and PFKP, pivotal genes associated with glycolysis, was observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Among 7,136 peaks in ChIP-seq analysis, 59 differentially upregulated peaks and 316 downregulated peaks were detected in IS-trained cells.
source: Among 7,136 peaks, 59 differentially upregulated peaks and 316 downregulated peaks were detected in IS-trained cells (Figure 3E and Table 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3E and Table 1.

claim: Activation of the innate immune response and positive regulation of the defense response were identified as major processes in IS-mediated trained immunity via GO biological process analysis.
source: Activation of the innate immune response and positive regulation of the defense response were identified as major processes via Go biological process analysis.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by GO analysis of ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Genes involved in regulation of ornithine decarboxylase (ODC) and metabolism of polyamine were recognized as major gene sets via Reactome Gene Set analysis.
source: Further, genes involved in regulation of ornithine decarboxylase (ODC) and metabolism of polyamine were recognized as major gene sets via Reactome Gene Set analysis (Figure 3F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by Reactome Gene Set analysis shown in Figure 3F.

claim: H3K4me3 is elevated at the promoters of important target genes associated with activation of the innate immune response, such as IFI16, XRCC5, and PQBP1.
source: A genome browser snapshot showing H3K4me3 binding illustrates that H3K4me3 is elevated at the promoters of important target genes associated with activation of the innate immune response, such as IFI16 (interferon-gamma inducible protein 16), XRCC5 (X-ray repair cross-complementing 5), and PQBP1 (polyglutamine binding protein 1)
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: H3K4me3 is elevated at the promoters of genes linked to the regulation of ODC, such as PSMA1, PSMA3, and OAZ3.
source: A genome browser snapshot showing H3K4me3 binding illustrates that H3K4me3 is elevated at the promoters of important target genes associated with activation of the innate immune response, such as IFI16 (interferon-gamma inducible protein 16), XRCC5 (X-ray repair cross-complementing 5), and PQBP1 (polyglutamine binding protein 1) and genes linked to the regulation of ODC, such as PSMA1 (proteasome 20 S subunit alpha 1), PSMA3 (proteasome 20 S subunit alpha 3), and OAZ3 (Ornithine Decarboxylase Antizyme 3, a protein that negatively regulates ODC activity) (Figure 3G; Hardbower et al., 2017).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3G and citation to previous literature.

claim: Immunoblot analysis reveals persistent nuclear translocation of IS-mediated AhR even on day 6 (prior to re-stimulation with LPS).
source: Immunoblot analysis depicted in Figure 4A reveals persistent nuclear translocation of IS-mediated AhR even on day 6 (prior to re-stimulation with LPS), which was entirely inhibited by GNF351 treatment, an AhR antagonist, on day 6.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: GNF351 treatment entirely inhibited nuclear translocation of IS-mediated AhR on day 6.
source: Immunoblot analysis depicted in Figure 4A reveals persistent nuclear translocation of IS-mediated AhR even on day 6 (prior to re-stimulation with LPS), which was entirely inhibited by GNF351 treatment, an AhR antagonist, on day 6.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Inhibition of AhR by GNF351 during IS training suppressed the increase in production of TNF-α and IL-6 following LPS restimulation on day 6 in IS-trained cells.
source: Inhibition of AhR by GNF351 during IS training suppressed the increase in production of TNF-α and IL-6 following LPS restimulation on day 6 in IS-trained cells (Figure 4B and C)
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Enhancement of IL-1β and MCP-1 mRNA expression in IS-trained cells was completely inhibited by GNF351.
source: In addition to TNF-α and IL-6, enhancement of IL-1β and MCP-1 mRNA expression in IS-trained cells was also completely inhibited, whereas decreased IL-10 expression was completely reversed by GNF351 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Decreased IL-10 expression in IS-trained cells was completely reversed by GNF351.
source: In addition to TNF-α and IL-6, enhancement of IL-1β and MCP-1 mRNA expression in IS-trained cells was also completely inhibited, whereas decreased IL-10 expression was completely reversed by GNF351 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: FICZ-pretreated monocytes exhibited augmented expression of TNF-α and IL-6 in response to secondary stimulation with LPS compared to non-trained cells.
source: FICZ-pretreated monocytes exhibited augmented expression of TNF-α and IL-6 in response to secondary stimulation with LPS compared to non-trained cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Knockdown of AhR suppressed the expression of TNF-α and IL-6 in IS-trained cells.
source: Additionally, knockdown of AhR suppressed the expression of TNF-α and IL-6 in IS-trained cells (Figure 4E)
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Enrichment of H3K4m3 on TNFA and IL6 promoters in IS-trained macrophages was inhibited by GNF351.
source: Our ChIP-qPCR assay showed that enrichment of H3K4m3 on TNFA and IL6 promoters in IS-trained macrophages was inhibited by GNF351 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: GNF351 has no effect on metabolic rewiring, including enhanced glycolysis and mitochondrial respiration, in IS-trained cells on day 6.
source: Of note, assessment of the metabolic profile by measuring ECAR and OCR illustrates that GNF351 has no effect on metabolic rewiring, including enhanced glycolysis and mitochondrial respiration, in IS-trained cells on day 6 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by Seahorse metabolic analysis data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: GNF351 had no inhibitory effect on IS-mediated enhancement of S6K activity.
source: This finding was corroborated by the immunoblotting data, which showed GNF351 had no inhibitory effect on IS-mediated enhancement of S6K activity, which is critical for inducing the aerobic glycolysis in human monocytes/macrophages (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: A total of 218 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), consisting of 71 upregulated and 147 downregulated genes, were identified in IS-trained macrophages compared to non-trained cells by RNA-seq.
source: A total of 218 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), consisting of 71 upregulated and 147 downregulated genes, were identified in IS-trained macrophages compared to non-trained cells (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; FC ≥± 2, <0.05).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: IS-trained macrophages had upregulated pathways including those involved in neutrophil degranulation, integrin cell surface interactions, extracellular matrix organization and AA metabolism.
source: IS-trained macrophages had upregulated pathways including those involved in neutrophil degranulation, integrin cell surface interactions, extracellular matrix organization and AA metabolism, whereas pathways associated with kinesins, cell cycle, and the Gα(i) signaling pathway were downregulated (Figure 5B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Pathways associated with kinesins, cell cycle, and the Gα(i) signaling pathway were downregulated in IS-trained macrophages.
source: IS-trained macrophages had upregulated pathways including those involved in neutrophil degranulation, integrin cell surface interactions, extracellular matrix organization and AA metabolism, whereas pathways associated with kinesins, cell cycle, and the Gα(i) signaling pathway were downregulated (Figure 5B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Genes related to AA metabolism were enriched in IS-trained macrophages compared to non-trained cells.
source: Our findings were supported by Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) using Molecular Signatures Database (MsigDB), in which genes related to AA metabolism were enriched in IS-trained macrophages compared to non-trained cells
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by GSEA shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Upregulated expression of AA metabolism-related genes was inhibited by treatment with GNF351.
source: Our findings were supported by Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) using Molecular Signatures Database (MsigDB), in which genes related to AA metabolism were enriched in IS-trained macrophages compared to non-trained cells and more importantly, upregulated expression of these genes was inhibited by treatment with GNF351 as illustrated by heatmap analysis of major genes related to AA metabolism (Figure 5C and D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by GSEA and heatmap analysis shown in Figure 5C, D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The leukotriene metabolic process, but not the cyclooxygenase (COX) pathway, was primarily involved in the induction of IS-mediated trained immunity.
source: Among AA metabolism pathways, the leukotriene metabolic process, but not the cyclooxygenase (COX) pathway, was primarily involved in the induction of IS-mediated trained immunity (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by GSEA shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The mRNA expression of ALOX5 and ALOX5AP was higher in IS-trained macrophages than non-trained cells.
source: The mRNA expression of arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase (ALOX5: also known as 5-LOX or 5-LO) and ALOX5 activating protein (ALOX5AP: also known as FLAP), the enzymes catalyzing AA into leukotrienes (a group of pro-inflammatory lipid mediators) (Salina et al., 2020; Rådmark et al., 2007; Pernet et al., 2019), was higher in IS-trained macrophages than non-trained cells.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The mRNA expression of LTB4R1, a high-affinity receptor for leukotriene B4 (LTB4), was upregulated in IS-trained macrophages.
source: In addition, the mRNA expression of LTB4R1 (also known as BLT1), a high-affinity receptor for leukotriene B4 (LTB4), was also upregulated.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The augmented expression of ALOX5, ALOX5AP, and LTB4R1 was repressed by GNF351 pretreatment.
source: The augmented expression of these AA metabolism-related genes was repressed by GNF351 pretreatment as shown by changes in expression of CYP1B1, a typical AhR target gene.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Immunoblot analysis validated the upregulation of ALOX5 and ALOX5AP expression in IS-trained immunity at the protein level.
source: Immunoblot analysis validated the upregulation of ALOX5 and ALOX5AP expression in IS-trained immunity, which was subsequently inhibited by GNF351 at the protein level (Figure 5F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Upregulation of ALOX5 and ALOX5AP expression in IS-trained immunity was inhibited by GNF351 at the protein level.
source: Immunoblot analysis validated the upregulation of ALOX5 and ALOX5AP expression in IS-trained immunity, which was subsequently inhibited by GNF351 at the protein level (Figure 5F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Knockdown of AhR suppressed the IS-induced mRNA expression of ALOX5, ALOX5AP, and LTB4R on day 6.
source: Furthermore, knockdown of AhR suppressed the IS-induced mRNA expression of ALOX5, ALOX5AP, and LTB4R on day 6 (Figure 5G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Treatment with FICZ elicited increased expression of ALOX5 and ALOX5AP.
source: Treatment with FICZ, an AhR agonist known to induce trained immunity (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), elicited increased expression of ALOX5 and ALOX5AP
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Treatment with KA did not result in elevation of ALOX5 and ALOX5AP.
source: while treatment with KA, a major protein-bound uremic toxin that does not induce trained immunity (Figure 1A), did not result in elevation of these genes
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The expression of ALOX5 and LTB4R1 is enhanced in IS-trained macrophages and ex vivo monocytes of ESRD patients.
source: Comparison of the fold changes of RNA-Seq data in the present study and microarray data reported previously (GSE155326) revealed that the expression of ALOX5 and LTB4R1 is enhanced in IS-trained macrophages and ex vivo monocytes of ESRD patients (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by comparison of RNA-seq and microarray data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: IS-induced TNF-α and IL-6 production were largely suppressed by zileuton.
source: We found that IS-induced TNF-α and IL-6 production were largely suppressed by both zileuton and U75302 (Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: IS-induced TNF-α and IL-6 production were largely suppressed by U75302.
source: We found that IS-induced TNF-α and IL-6 production were largely suppressed by both zileuton and U75302 (Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Knockdown of ALOX5 inhibited IS-induced expression of TNF-α and IL-6.
source: Additionally, knockdown of ALOX5 inhibited IS-induced expression of TNF-α and IL-6 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The enrichment of H3K4me3 on TNFA and IL6 promoters in IS-trained macrophages was inhibited by zileuton.
source: Our results demonstrated that the enrichment of H3K4me3 on TNFA and IL6 promoters in IS-trained macrophages was inhibited by zileuton, although phosphorylation of S6K remained unaffected (Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Phosphorylation of S6K remained unaffected by zileuton treatment in IS-trained macrophages.
source: Our results demonstrated that the enrichment of H3K4me3 on TNFA and IL6 promoters in IS-trained macrophages was inhibited by zileuton, although phosphorylation of S6K remained unaffected (Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1I.

claim: The expression of ALOX5, ALOX5AP, and LTB4R1 mRNA was augmented by training with pooled uremic sera of ESRD patients compared with HCs.
source: The expression of ALOX5, ALOX5AP, and LTB4R1 mRNA was augmented by training with pooled uremic sera of ESRD patients compared with HCs (Figure 5J)
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: Augmented expression of ALOX5, ALOX5AP, and LTB4R1 by training with pooled uremic sera was maintained after re-stimulation with LPS.
source: The expression of ALOX5, ALOX5AP, and LTB4R1 mRNA was augmented by training with pooled uremic sera of ESRD patients compared with HCs (Figure 5J), and this augmented expression was maintained after re-stimulation with LPS (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1J.

claim: RNA-Seq data of IS-trained macrophages showed no obvious change in the expression profile of major histone-modifying enzymes.
source: However, RNA-Seq data of IS-trained macrophages showed no obvious change in the expression profile of major histone-modifying enzymes (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: mRNA expression of major histone modifying enzymes including KDM5A, KDM5B, KDM5C, SETDB2, SETD7, and SETD3 were not changed in IS-trained macrophages on day 6.
source: In agreement with this, mRNA expression of major histone modifying enzymes including KDM5A, KDM5B, KDM5C, SETDB2, SETD7, and SETD3 were not changed in IS-trained macrophages on day 6 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B; Arts et al., 2016b; Kimball et al., 2019; Zhong et al., 2018; Keating et al., 2020).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and citations to previous literature.

claim: Treatment with MTA partially inhibited expression of ALOX5 and ALOX5AP mRNA.
source: Treatment with MTA, a non-selective methyltransferase inhibitor, partially inhibited expression of ALOX5 and ALOX5AP mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C)
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: There is a significant positive correlation between H3K4me3 enrichment and gene expression in IS-trained macrophages.
source: Ultimately, to validate the association between ChIP-Seq and RNA-Seq data, we employed Spearman's correlation for comparative analysis and conducted linear regression to ascertain the presence of a consistent global trend in RNA expression. Our findings unveiled a significant positive correlation, underscoring the consistent relationship between H3K4me3 enrichment and gene expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Ex vivo monocytes of ESRD patients had a higher production of TNF-α after LPS stimulation than those of HCs.
source: Ex vivo monocytes of ESRD patients had a higher production of TNF-α and mRNA expression of IL-1β and MCP-1 after LPS stimulation than those of HCs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C and Table 2).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Ex vivo monocytes of ESRD patients had higher mRNA expression of IL-1β and MCP-1 after LPS stimulation than those of HCs.
source: Ex vivo monocytes of ESRD patients had a higher production of TNF-α and mRNA expression of IL-1β and MCP-1 after LPS stimulation than those of HCs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–C and Table 2).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Monocytes of ESRD patients, which were trained by resting in the culture media for 6 days, significantly augmented production of TNF-α and IL-6 upon LPS stimulation compared to those from HCs.
source: More importantly, monocytes of ESRD patients, which were trained by resting in the culture media for 6 days, significantly augmented production of TNF-α and IL-6 and expression of IL-1β mRNA upon LPS stimulation compared to those from HCs (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6A-C.

claim: Monocytes of ESRD patients trained for 6 days significantly augmented expression of IL-1β mRNA upon LPS stimulation compared to those from HCs.
source: More importantly, monocytes of ESRD patients, which were trained by resting in the culture media for 6 days, significantly augmented production of TNF-α and IL-6 and expression of IL-1β mRNA upon LPS stimulation compared to those from HCs (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6A-C.

claim: The expression of ALOX5 in ex vivo monocytes of ESRD patients was significantly increased at the protein level compared with that of age-matched HCs.
source: Consistent with our findings (Figure 5), the expression of ALOX5 in ex vivo monocytes of ESRD patients was significantly increased at the protein level compared with that of age-matched HCs (Figure 6D–F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6D-F.

claim: Monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) from ESRD patients had higher expression of ALOX5 compared to MDMs of HCs.
source: Moreover, monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) from ESRD patients also had higher expression of ALOX5 compared to MDMs of HCs (Figure 6G and H)
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6G and H.

claim: The level of TNF-α in serum was increased in IS-trained mice compared to that of control mice.
source: The level of TNF-α in serum was increased in IS-trained mice compared to that of control mice (Figure 6J).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6J.

claim: The amount of TNF-α and IL-6 in the supernatant was augmented following culture with LPS-stimulated mouse splenic myeloid cells derived from IS-trained mice compared to the control condition.
source: The amount of TNF-α and IL-6 in the supernatant was augmented following culture with LPS-stimulated mouse splenic myeloid cells derived from IS-trained mice compared the control condition (Figure 6K).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6K.

claim: Upregulation of ALOX5 expression was observed in ex vivo splenic myeloid cells of IS-treated mice compared to control mice.
source: Additionally, we observed upregulation of ALOX5 expression in ex vivo splenic myeloid cells of IS-treated mice compared to control mice (Figure 6L and M)
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6L and M.

claim: Treatment with zileuton inhibited the production of TNF-α and IL-6 in ex vivo splenic myeloid cells of IS-trained mice.
source: Finally, treatment with zileuton, an ALOX5 inhibitor, inhibited the production of TNF-α and IL-6 in ex vivo splenic myeloid cells of IS-trained mice (Figure 6N).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6N.

claim: BMDM from IS-trained mice did not exhibit heightened production of TNF-α and IL-6.
source: It was observed that BMDM from IS-trained mice did not exhibit heightened production of TNF-α and IL-6, and the expression level of ALOX5 in bone marrow progenitor cells remained unaltered when compared to non-trained cells, indicating that our acute IS-trained mice did not induce central trained immunity (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and E; Kaufmann et al., 2018; Riksen et al., 2023).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and citations to previous literature.

claim: The expression level of ALOX5 in bone marrow progenitor cells from IS-trained mice remained unaltered when compared to non-trained cells.
source: It was observed that BMDM from IS-trained mice did not exhibit heightened production of TNF-α and IL-6, and the expression level of ALOX5 in bone marrow progenitor cells remained unaltered when compared to non-trained cells, indicating that our acute IS-trained mice did not induce central trained immunity (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and E; Kaufmann et al., 2018; Riksen et al., 2023).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Results section and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E and citations to previous literature.

claim: The acute IS-trained mice model did not induce central trained immunity.
source: It was observed that BMDM from IS-trained mice did not exhibit heightened production of TNF-α and IL-6, and the expression level of ALOX5 in bone marrow progenitor cells remained unaltered when compared to non-trained cells, indicating that our acute IS-trained mice did not induce central trained immunity (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and E; Kaufmann et al., 2018; Riksen et al., 2023).
evidence: This interpretation is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and E and citations to previous literature.

claim: In addition to pathogenic stimuli, endogenous sterile inflammatory insults including ox-LDL, hyperglycemia and uric acid, trigger trained immunity and contribute to chronic inflammation in cardiovascular diseases and gout.
source: Recent studies have reported that in addition to pathogenic stimuli, endogenous sterile inflammatory insults including ox-LDL, hyperglycemia and uric acid, also trigger trained immunity and contribute to chronic inflammation in cardiovascular diseases and gout (Christ et al., 2018; Edgar et al., 2021; Bekkering et al., 2014; Cabău et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: IS provokes trained immunity in human monocytes/macrophage through epigenetic modification, metabolic rewiring, and AhR-dependent induction of the AA pathway.
source: In the present study, we provide evidence that IS, a major uremic toxin, provokes trained immunity in human monocytes/macrophage through epigenetic modification, metabolic rewiring, and AhR-dependent induction of the AA pathway
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study as stated in the Discussion section, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: CKD is associated with increased risk factors of CVD including traditional risk factors, such as hypertension, age and dyslipidemia, as well as non-traditional risk factors, such as oxidative stress and inflammation.
source: CKD is associated with increased risk factors of CVD including traditional risk factors, such as hypertension, age and dyslipidemia, as well as non-traditional risk factors, such as oxidative stress and inflammation (Lim et al., 2021; Menon et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: CKD is an independent risk factor for CVD.
source: Further, recent cohort studies have shown that CKD is an independent risk factor for CVD (Menon et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Uremia accompanying renal failure causes immune dysfunction, which is closely linked to the pathogenesis of CKD-related CVD.
source: Uremia accompanying renal failure causes immune dysfunction, which is closely linked to the pathogenesis of CKD-related CVD (Betjes, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: IS is a prototypical protein-bound uremic toxin most likely to be participating in progressive pathophysiology of CVD including endothelial dysfunction, vascular calcification, and increased atherosclerosis.
source: Among over 100 uremic toxins identified, IS is a prototypical protein-bound uremic toxin most likely to be participating in progressive pathophysiology of CVD including endothelial dysfunction, vascular calcification, and increased atherosclerosis (Kim et al., 2017; Nakano et al., 2019; Hung et al., 2017; Leong and Sirich, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A prolonged hyperactivation of trained immunity is intimately related to the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis, the major contributor to cardiovascular diseases.
source: Mounting evidence suggests that a prolonged hyperactivation of trained immunity is intimately related to the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis, the major contributor to cardiovascular diseases.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge based on mounting evidence.

claim: Oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL), hyperglycemia, and the Western diet have been reported to induce trained immunity through epigenetic reprogramming.
source: Oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL), hyperglycemia, and the estern diet, all known to be associate with the progression of atherosclerosis, have been reported to induce trained immunity through epigenetic reprogramming (Christ et al., 2018; Edgar et al., 2021; Bekkering et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: IS is difficult to clear by hemodialysis.
source: Given that IS is difficult to clear by hemodialysis, this toxin has a chronic effect on the immune system of patients.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge in the Discussion section.

claim: The induction of trained immunity is coordinated through the interplay of epigenetic modifications and metabolic rewiring.
source: Mechanistic studies have demonstrated that the induction of trained immunity is coordinated through the interplay of epigenetic modifications and metabolic rewiring, which is broadly characterized as prolonged changes in transcription programs and cell physiology that do not involve permanent genetic changes, such as the mutations and recombination events crucial for adaptive immunity (Netea et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: AhR is a ligand-activated nuclear transcription factor, which is activated by several exogenous compounds and multiple endogenous ligands including tryptophan and indole metabolites.
source: AhR is a ligand-activated nuclear transcription factor (TF), which is activated by several exogenous compounds, such as benzo[a]pyrene environmental pollutants and 2,3,7,8-tetrachloro-dibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD), as well as by multiple endogenous ligands including tryptophan and indole metabolites (Rothhammer and Quintana, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: AhR plays a multifaceted role in modulating cellular mechanisms such as inflammation, cell growth, and antioxidant responses.
source: AhR plays a multifaceted role in modulating cellular mechanisms such as inflammation, cell growth, and antioxidant responses (Stockinger et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: AhR is expressed by various immune cells, and its signaling exerts integrative effects on the cellular environment and metabolism of the immune responses.
source: AhR is expressed by various immune cells, and its signaling exerts integrative effects on the cellular environment and metabolism of the immune responses (Gutiérrez-Vázquez and Quintana, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Metabolic rewiring, especially upregulation of aerobic glycolysis, is a major mechanism underlying the induction of trained immunity via regulation of epigenetic modification by metabolites.
source: Metabolic rewiring, especially upregulation of aerobic glycolysis, is known as a major mechanism underlying the induction of trained immunity via regulation of epigenetic modification by metabolites, such as mevalonate and fumarate generated from this metabolic rewiring (Bekkering et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Immune priming long non-coding RNAs (IPLs) induce epigenetic reprogramming by influencing 3D nuclear architecture.
source: Furthermore, in addition to establishing the bidirectional link between heightened glycolysis and activating histone modifications, as evidenced by the suppression of histone modification by 2DG, a glycolysis inhibitor, in IS-induced immunity (Figure 3D), recent studies have demonstrated that immune priming long non-coding RNAs (IPLs) also induce epigenetic reprogramming by influencing 3D nuclear architecture (Netea et al., 2020; Fanucchi et al., 2021)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: RUNX1, a transcription factor, contributes to the induction of trained immunity by overexpression of RUNX1 target genes.
source: and that RUNX1, a transcription factor, contributes to the induction of trained immunity by overexpression of RUNX1 target genes (Edgar et al., 2021)
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to recent literature.

claim: Inducers of trained immunity, such as β-glucan, BCG, uric acid, and oxLDL, initiate intracellular signaling and metabolic pathways via different receptors, but the most common pathway is the Akt/mTOR/HIF1α-dependent induction of aerobic glycolysis.
source: Although inducers of trained immunity, such as β-glucan, BCG, uric acid, and oxLDL, initiate intracellular signaling and metabolic pathways, each via different receptors, the most common pathway is the Akt/mTOR/HIF1α-dependent induction of aerobic glycolysis (Netea et al., 2020; Mulder et al., 2019; Bekkering et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: IS activates mTORC1 in a variety of cells such as epithelial cells, fibroblasts, and THP-1 cells mainly via the organic anion transporters (OAT)/NADPH oxidase/ROS pathway, but not the AhR pathway.
source: Recent studies have shown that IS activates mTORC1 in a variety of cells such as epithelial cells, fibroblasts, and THP-1 cells mainly via the organic anion transporters (OAT)/NADPH oxidase/ROS pathway, but not the AhR pathway (Nakano et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to recent literature.

claim: IS-trained macrophages acquire the characteristics of trained immunity by AhR-dependent and -independent mechanisms.
source: Our findings suggest that IS-trained macrophages acquire the characteristics of trained immunity by AhR-dependent and -independent mechanisms and enhances proinflammatory responses upon secondary stimulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings stated in the Discussion section, supported by experimental data.

claim: ALOX5 and ALOX5AP are major rate-limiting enzymes associated with the AA pathway, involved in the production of leukotrienes.
source: ALOX5 and ALOX5AP are major rate-limiting enzymes associated with the AA pathway, involved in the production of leukotrienes, proinflammatory lipid mediators derived from AA (Rådmark et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Leukotriene B4 (LTB4) is an extremely potent inflammatory mediator that binds to G-protein-coupled protein, LTB4R, and enhances inflammatory responses by increased phagocytosis and activation of the signaling pathway for the production of cytokines.
source: Among leukotrienes, leukotriene B4 (LTB4), an extremely potent inflammatory mediator, binds to Gprotein-coupled protein, LTB4R, and enhances inflammatory responses by increased phagocytosis and activation of the signaling pathway for the production of cytokines (Salina et al., 2020; Pernet et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The LTB4-LTB4R signaling pathway induces the PI3K/Akt or NF-κB pathways.
source: Mechanistically, the LTB4-LTB4R signaling pathway induces the PI3K/Akt or NF-κB pathways (Ihara et al., 2007; Tong et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: AhR-dependent LTB4 production through enhanced ALOX5 expression in hepatocytes induces hepatotoxicity via neutrophil infiltration.
source: AhR-dependent LTB4 production through enhanced ALOX5 expression in hepatocytes reportedly induces hepatotoxicity via neutrophil infiltration (Takeda et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The increase in ALOX5 activity and LTB4 expression has been reported in patients with ESRD.
source: The increase in ALOX5 activity and LTB4 expression has been reported in patients with ESRD (Maccarrone et al., 2002; Maccarrone et al., 2001; Montford et al., 2019)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ALOX5 mediates mitochondrial damage and apoptosis in mononuclear cells of ESRD patients.
source: and ALOX5 mediates mitochondrial damage and apoptosis in mononuclear cells of ESRD patients (Maccarrone et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Antagonists of ALOX5/ALOX5AP have been used for treatment in CKD.
source: Thus, antagonists of ALOX5/ALOX5AP have been used for treatment in CKD (Montford et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Increased ALOX5 in monocytes and macrophages of ESRD patients is likely mediated by IS in uremic serum.
source: Considering that pretreatment with the uremic serum of ESRD patients elicits a change in gene expression and cytokine production as observed in IS-trained macrophages, it is likely that increased ALOX5 in monocytes and macrophages of ESRD patients is mediated by IS in uremic serum.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Discussion section based on experimental findings.

claim: Trained immunity of macrophages is implicated in the pathogenesis of CVD, such as atherosclerosis.
source: Recent studies have demonstrated that trained immunity of macrophages is implicated in the pathogenesis of CVD, such as atherosclerosis (Edgar et al., 2021; Bekkering et al., 2014; van der Valk et al., 2016; Mulder et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: When ESRD monocytes exposed to IS in the circulation enter atherosclerotic plaques and differentiate into macrophages, they are no longer exposed to IS, because IS is protein-bound and hence not expected to be present in the plaque microenvironment.
source: However, when ESRD monocytes exposed to the IS in the circulation enter atherosclerotic plaques and differentiate into macrophages, they are no longer exposed to IS, because this is protein-bound and hence not expected to the present in the plaque microenvironment.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation stated in the Discussion section to reconcile the chronic exposure to IS with the trained immunity model.

claim: Murine models have been widely used to investigate the specific contribution of inducers of trained immunity and the underlying mechanisms to a long-term functional modification of innate cells in vivo.
source: Murine models have been widely used to investigate the specific contribution of inducers of trained immunity and the underlying mechanisms to a long-term functional modification of innate cells in vivo (Saeed et al., 2014; Keating et al., 2020; Garcia-Valtanen et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mice trained with β-glucan enhance the production of proinflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β by monocytes and macrophages in response to secondary microbial stimuli.
source: Mice trained with β-glucan enhance the production of proinflammatory cytokines such as TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β by monocytes and macrophages in response to secondary microbial stimuli and subsequently obtain increased protection against various microbial infections (Mulder et al., 2019; Bekkering et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Intraperitoneal injection of exogenous IS into wild-type C57BL/6 mice leads to an increase of IS in the plasma until 3~6 hr post-injection despite its rapid excretion by the kidney.
source: Previous studies have shown that intraperitoneal injection of exogenous IS into wild-type C57BL/6 mice leads to an increase of IS in the plasma until 3~6 hr post-injection despite its rapid excretion by the kidney.
evidence: This statement is presented as a finding from previous studies.

claim: During the period of increased IS in plasma after intraperitoneal injection, the expression of pro-inflammatory, pro-oxidant, and pro-apoptotic genes in peritoneal macrophages was upregulated.
source: In this period, the expression of pro-inflammatory, pro-oxidant, and pro-apoptotic genes in peritoneal macrophages was upregulated (Nakano et al., 2021; Rapa et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Intraperitoneal injection of IS daily for 3 days elevates IS in the plasma of mice and activates the mTORC1 signaling pathway in the mouse kidney.
source: Moreover, intraperitoneal injection of IS daily for 3 days elevates IS in the plasma of mice and activates the mTORC1 signaling pathway in the mouse kidney (Nakano et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The IS-injected mouse model is suitable for investigating the mechanisms underlying IS-mediated immune responses.
source: This suggests that the IS-injected mouse model is suitable for investigating the mechanisms underlying IS-mediated immune responses.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Discussion section based on previous findings.

claim: IS plays an important role in the induction of trained immunity, which is critical in inflammatory immune responses in patients with CKD.
source: These results suggest that IS plays an important role in the induction of trained immunity, which is critical in inflammatory immune responses in patients with CKD and thus, it holds potential as a therapeutic target.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study as stated in the Discussion section, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: IS holds potential as a therapeutic target in CKD.
source: These results suggest that IS plays an important role in the induction of trained immunity, which is critical in inflammatory immune responses in patients with CKD and thus, it holds potential as a therapeutic target.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about therapeutic implications based on the study findings.
